neighbours.label: the comparison word (' as', ' than') that puts the subject on a level with something bad: 'as bad ⟦as⟧', 'no better ⟦than⟧', 'in the same league ⟦as⟧'; neutral comparisons stay quiet
fire: For the villagers, losing the well was as bad as losing the harvest.
The judge said the forger was no better than a pickpocket.
Voters place the minister in the same camp as the swindlers.
To her, breaking a promise is as shameful as telling a lie.
The coach called the referee no different than a paid cheat.
Many readers put the pamphlet in the same class as cheap propaganda.
The reviewer found the sequel as dreadful as the original.
He treats his rivals as no better than vermin.
quiet: For the villagers, the new well was as deep as the old one.
The judge said the clerk was taller than the bailiff.
Voters see the minister as a careful planner.
To her, the morning walk is as pleasant as breakfast.
The coach worked as a referee before he retired.
Many readers bought the pamphlet as soon as it appeared.
The reviewer found the sequel as long as the original.
He greets his rivals as they arrive at the hall.

notes: Card: 'as mad⟦ as⟧ that', 'as bad⟦ as⟧ meat', 'no different⟦ than⟧ an armed robber', 'same class⟦ as⟧', 'as unappealing⟦ as⟧'; the output promotes ' beyond', ' unknown', ' foreign', ' outside' and suppresses ' within', ' legitimate', ' fellow'. Probes: 'no better than thieves' 0.86, 'as bad as cheating' 0.78, 'same league as' 0.51, 'as harmful as' 0.33, 'same category as' 0.21, but 'as bright as' 0.01, 'twice as tall as' 0.01, 'worked as' 0.01, 'similar to' 0.02, 'no different than' 0.06. So the comparison word fires when the equation is a put-down; near misses are neutral comparisons and other uses of 'as'.
